item.title: CUDA Unified Memory: One Pointer, Two Processors
item.description:
CUDA Unified Memory: One Pointer, Two Processors

The previous note covered explicit CUDA streams and how to overlap host-device transfers with computation. This note covers Unified Memory, an alternative to explicit cudaMalloc / cudaMemcpy / cudaFree. It lets both CPU and GPU use a single pointer, at the cost of some performance complexity under the hood.

Unified Memory is seductive: it removes the need to think about host and device pointers separately. But it does not remove the physical reality that CPU and GPU memory are separate. Understanding when it helps and when it hurts is essential.
